records.collection_title: Louisiana Historical Society (Papers of Robert Glenk)
records.collection_description: Correspondence (1877–1939), minutes (1897–1919), announcements, invitations, membership lists and committee reports; the finding aid says most is arranged and additional items belonging to the record group were later identified and placed in the collection.
records.scope_relevance: High retrieval relevance for the Louisiana Historical Society's 1903 colonial loan-exhibit records; no item-level register, correspondence or disposition record for item 345 is identified in this finding aid.
records.next_action: Request RG23 accession T025.2003.13 folders or register entries for the 1903 colonial exhibit, especially catalogue items 342 and 345; seek loan register, correspondence/minutes and post-exhibit disposition.

records.collection_description: The collection-level inventory describes varied Louisiana history materials, including land-grant requests, divorce material, David Morgan/Battle of New Orleans items, a Bible Society ledger, emancipation/purchase/mortgage documents, plantation records, Civil War materials and later ephemera; it does not itemize the 24 February 1731 debt decree.
records.scope_relevance: Related collector/loan collection is a possible provenance inquiry, but no item-level link to the 1903 exhibit's debt decree is established. The date range and summary are not a complete item-level inventory.
records.next_action: Request the accession/item inventory and loan-resolution file for RG431; ask whether the 1903 item 345 was part of this loan, transferred, returned or separately disposed, without assuming any outcome.

records.collection_description: The 2025 finding aid describes miscellaneous letters/manuscripts, mostly 19th-century, open for research with digitized items available on request; majority gifted by the Cusachs Estate in 1930, remainder purchased in 2017. Its oversize list includes a 1763 indenture, accession 09894.117, outside the stated date range. No 1731 debt decree or connection to the 1903 exhibit copy is itemized.
records.scope_relevance: Strong retrieval route for exhibit-related documentation: the finding aid lists a 1903 invitation to Gaspar Cusachs for the Louisiana Historical Society colonial-museum opening and several 1903/1904 exhibit-related invitations. These invitation records do not link RG112 to debt-decree item 345 or establish loan, ownership, or present custody.
records.date_range_exception: The finding aid lists a 1763 indenture (09894.117) despite its stated 1770–1904 range, so date range is not a strict lower bound and cannot be used to infer absence of earlier material.
records.next_action: Request RG112 folders 15, 17, 18, 20 and 21 (accessions 2017.001.07.1, .07.3, .07.4a-c, .08.2 and .08.3) for scans and any attached exhibit correspondence. Search RG23 for the 1903 item 345 loan/register/disposition and ask whether it was associated with RG431/RG112; do not infer a link from invitations.

related_items.description: Invitation issued to Gaspar Cusachs by the Louisiana Historical Society for opening ceremonies of the colonial museum at the Ursuline Convent.
Invitation from the governor to a celebration of the 100th anniversary of the transfer of Louisiana from France to the United States.
Invitation and two tickets issued to Mr. and Mrs. Gaspar Cusachs for a costume ball at the French Opera House celebrating the Louisiana Transfer centennial.
Invitation to a reception honoring a French delegate and Governor Newton C. Blanchard, given by the French Exposition of Louisiana.
Invitation to Louisiana Day at the Cabildo, issued by the Louisiana State Commission for the Louisiana Purchase Exposition in St. Louis.

limitations: These are institutional collection-level finding aids, not item-level inventories or examination of the decree.
The 1903 catalogue's Owner column attributes item 345 to Mr. Gaspar Cusachs historically; it does not establish present custody or a complete chain of custody.
RG23 is a retrieval route for the Louisiana Historical Society's exhibit records, not evidence the 1731 print is in RG23.
RG431 and RG112 are separate collection descriptions; no object-level connection between either and the 1903 item 345 is established.
RG112 lists a 1763 item outside its stated 1770–1904 date range, so collection date ranges cannot be used as proof of absence.
No physical object, accession inventory, loan register, disposition record, current custody, original legal text, liability allocation or payment was examined or verified.
